question: Island regions are particularly exposed to the threat of water scarcity.1 The limited water resources are under pressure due to the impacts of the climate crisis, intensifying periods of drought, outdated water supply networks and significant seasonal population increases due to tourism.

2 On most islands, which are popular tourist destinations, natural water reserves are insufficient, leading to costly and energy-intensive solutions, such as reliance on water imports and conventional desalination plants.

Taking into account the Parliament's position on water resilience, which calls for special treatment of islands due to their vulnerability and for the removal of barriers to access to financial support for local and regional investments in water management and infrastructure,3 the need for integrated rainwater collection and storage systems, modern desalination plants with renewable energy sources, smart water management networks with real-time leakage detection, wastewater reuse systems for irrigation and smart demand management systems,4 as well as the need for enhanced participation of island authorities in decision-making on infrastructure planning: 1.

Does the Commission intend to recognise addressing water scarcity on islands as a strategic priority and to incorporate a specific pillar on water security and resilience in the forthcoming European strategy for islands?

Does the Commission intend to support the creation of a new specific financial instrument in the new MFF for investments in sustainable, resilient solutions and infrastructure for integrated water management on islands?

Water scarcity is becoming a systemic phenomenon and a significant limiting factor for economic development. 2 According to official data, approximately 30 % of the European population lives in areas with permanent water stress and up to 70 % in areas with seasonal stress during the summer period (https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/analysis/indicators/use-of-freshwater-resources-in-europe-1).

Notably, in Greece last year, dozens of island municipalities were placed in a state of emergency due to water scarcity, while today many islands are in this situation already. Seven Greek islands are already in a state of emergency due to water scarcity. 3 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0091_EL.html. 4 See e.g. the INSULEUR proposals, https://ec.europa.
eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-yoursay/initiatives/16992-Στρατηγικη-της-ΕΕ-για-της-ΕΕ-για-τα-νησια/F33386921_el. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) The EU strategy for islands1 recognises that islands face water-related challenges and recommends that Member States prioritise investments in water infrastructure to improve water services and distribution networks and increase water saving and water reuse, while restoring natural water retention.

Cohesion policy supports such investments by strengthening water resilience and sustainable water management. Reflecting the growing importance of water resilience, the mid-term review of cohesion policy2 encouraged Member States to increase investments in sustainable water management, increased water efficiency, secure access to water and measures enhancing water resilience, resulting in the reallocation of EUR 1.

6 billion to islands through cohesion policy programmes, including EUR 158 million for water-related investments. The proposal for the next Multiannual Financial Framework3 provides that at least 35% of the EU budget should contribute to climate and environmental objectives, including water resilience, while continuing to support research and innovation projects that accelerate the green transition.

Water resilience is also reflected in the main funding programmes, in shared management, under the EU’s proposed next long-term budget. It is an important element of the National and Regional Partnership Plans, with a climate and environmental contribution of at least 43%, which aim to ensure sustainable prosperity across all regions and maintain quality of life across the EU4.
The European Competitiveness Fund5 will also support water resilience and the transition to a water-smart economy, through its clean Transition and Industrial Decarbonisation window.
